statusDetail: Coverage-complete report-mode audit across six representative paths.

page.notes: Public Tamil-dubbed movie catalogue. No local source was supplied. The download journey was inspected through the final file-choice page without downloading media.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Dark emulation leaves all sampled surfaces light and root color-scheme is normal.
No active animations were present on sampled routes under reduced motion; getAnimations() returned an empty array.

checkOutcomes.method: Contrast emulation, CSS probe, and Lighthouse
checkOutcomes.evidence: No prefers-contrast/forced-colors rules were found and known contrast failures remain.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM/CSS inspection across representative navigation flow
checkOutcomes.evidence: The MPA route journey has no @view-transition opt-in and swaps documents abruptly.
No parallax, scrollytelling, entry reveal, or other scroll-linked motion exists on the representative templates.
checkOutcomes.reason: No parallax, scrollytelling, entry reveal, or other scroll-linked motion exists on the representative templates.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The catalogue exposes ordinary links only; there is no swipe, drag, pull, carousel, or gesture-driven surface to evaluate.
checkOutcomes.reason: The catalogue exposes ordinary links only; there is no swipe, drag, pull, carousel, or gesture-driven surface to evaluate.

checkOutcomes.method: Mobile layout metrics and CSS inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: The 4,161px homepage has no progress or scroll-state-aware chrome.
No tooltip, popover, menu, or other anchored overlay appears on the sampled templates.
checkOutcomes.reason: No tooltip, popover, menu, or other anchored overlay appears on the sampled templates.

checkOutcomes.method: Link-label probe and pagination DOM inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: Repeated generic actions and fragment pagination provide weak destination/current-state cues.

checkOutcomes.method: Desktop/mobile load screenshots and DOM overlay inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: Load screenshots show content immediately with no full-viewport modal, banner, or interstitial.
No overlays or disclosure controls are present, so there is no custom primitive to replace.
checkOutcomes.reason: No overlays or disclosure controls are present, so there is no custom primitive to replace.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Brand/search prompts, SEO prose, and Page Keywords blocks repeatedly compete with titles.
At 360px, home, listing, and detail all report 0px horizontal overflow with a viewport meta tag.
Shared folder/card/pagination components use viewport rules only; no container queries are authored.
Keyboard focus is visible, but many touch targets are only 14–17px high.
The first viewport clearly states that the site is a Tamil-dubbed movie catalogue and immediately offers recent titles.

checkOutcomes.method: End-to-end DOM walkthrough without downloading media
checkOutcomes.evidence: The download journey works to the final choice but requires several avoidable intermediate pages and generic labels.
A 404 produces a raw server page without recovery actions.

checkOutcomes.method: Two Lighthouse runs plus trace summary
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse LCP is 3.9–4.0s and detail CLS is 0.126; trace TBT is 0ms.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse layout-shift audit and image primitive
checkOutcomes.evidence: Detail CLS is 0.126 and the poster lacks intrinsic dimensions.
The trace recorded zero long tasks and 0ms total blocking time; Lighthouse TBT also passed.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR summary confirmed against DOM head markup and Lighthouse insights
checkOutcomes.evidence: CSS and imported fonts form a render-blocking chain with an estimated 1.9s saving.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR weight analysis and Lighthouse code audit
checkOutcomes.evidence: GTM transfers 152.8KB and Lighthouse estimates 67KiB unused JavaScript.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM probe, image primitive, and Lighthouse accessibility audits
checkOutcomes.evidence: Sampled interactive content uses native links with text, and all sampled images have non-empty alt text; there are no forms/canvas controls.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse contrast audit on home and detail
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse measured 3.79:1 red text and 2.7:1 white-on-blue text.
No main/nav landmark exists and the detail template has no h1; focus itself is visible.
Dense 14px keyword-heavy blocks and repetitive rows hinder scanning.
Reflow passes without overflow, but link hit areas remain 14–17px high.
Both Lighthouse runs passed the errors-in-console audit; no uncaught exception was reported.
Doctype/charset pass, but sampled poster and folder images omit intrinsic dimensions and responsive sources.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse diagnostics and HAR hygiene signals
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse reports BFCache/Inspector issues and HAR records an ad script blocked by ORB.
Home, listing, and detail templates each expose descriptive titles and meta descriptions.

checkOutcomes.method: Link probe, DOM review, and robots fetch
checkOutcomes.evidence: Viewport and robots pass, but many links are generic and active pagination uses href="#".

checkOutcomes.method: Metadata probe plus direct robots/sitemap HTTP requests
checkOutcomes.evidence: Public pages return 200 and are allowed, but canonical links are absent and sitemap.xml returns 404.
Movie details provide rich visible entity data but no JSON-LD or Open Graph tags.

checkOutcomes.method: Headers, cookies, HAR, and secrets primitives
checkOutcomes.evidence: HTTPS passes, but all inspected defensive headers are absent and PHPSESSID lacks Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite protection.
Five third-party origins load, known analytics runs, and third parties transfer 178.3KB without an evident consent control.
No permission request, sign-in, account, or authentication surface appears in the representative scope.
checkOutcomes.reason: No permission request, sign-in, account, or authentication surface appears in the representative scope.

checkOutcomes.evidence: HSTS, clickjacking defense, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and CSP are absent.

checkOutcomes.method: Discoverability primitive with JS-disabled crawler screenshots
checkOutcomes.evidence: Raw server HTML contains 100% of rendered content words on home and detail; neither page is a JS shell.
The server-rendered link flow remains stable without overlays or fragile client state, and all intermediate pages rendered.
This is a content catalogue rather than an app-like tool; no install/offline intent is evident, so PWA installability is not required.
checkOutcomes.reason: This is a content catalogue rather than an app-like tool; no install/offline intent is evident, so PWA installability is not required.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The sampled HTTP 404 is an unstyled Apache dead end without recovery.
lang=en is set, but direction is implicit and shared CSS still uses physical left/right spacing.
Visible dates are plain locale-specific text with no time/datetime semantics or observable locale formatting.
The sampled catalogue exposes release/update dates only and no event time, appointment, recurring schedule, or timezone-sensitive instant.
checkOutcomes.reason: The sampled catalogue exposes release/update dates only and no event time, appointment, recurring schedule, or timezone-sensitive instant.

checkOutcomes.method: Link destination DOM review and HAR third-party inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: Telegram, Contact Us, and DMCA labels all route to home, while an opaque ad script loads.
No user-input form exists in the representative public catalogue flow.
checkOutcomes.reason: No user-input form exists in the representative public catalogue flow.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No address, payment, sign-in, signup, or other editable input exists in scope.
checkOutcomes.reason: No address, payment, sign-in, signup, or other editable input exists in scope.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No checkout, subscription, consent, authentication, or account-management flow exists in scope.
checkOutcomes.reason: No checkout, subscription, consent, authentication, or account-management flow exists in scope.

checkOutcomes.method: Image primitive and Lighthouse image delivery insight
checkOutcomes.evidence: Detail poster is an oversized legacy JPG with no srcset; Lighthouse estimates 65KiB savings.
Analytics/ad requests run before interaction and dominate the static page transfer.
Third-party code is 91.9% of total transferred bytes.
No declared intent indicates that this catalogue wants agents to perform structured actions; robots explicitly blocks major AI agents.
checkOutcomes.reason: No declared intent indicates that this catalogue wants agents to perform structured actions; robots explicitly blocks major AI agents.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No summarisation or generative user task is exposed, so built-in on-device inference is not required.
checkOutcomes.reason: No summarisation or generative user task is exposed, so built-in on-device inference is not required.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The site is a static multi-page catalogue with no modal, SPA route, feed expansion, editor, or representative same-page interaction to repeat ten times.
checkOutcomes.reason: The site is a static multi-page catalogue with no modal, SPA route, feed expansion, editor, or representative same-page interaction to repeat ten times.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The homepage snapshot is proportionate: 3.58MB self size, 82,873 heap nodes, about 3.5MB used JS heap, and only 220 DOM elements.

checkOutcomes.method: Heap constructor summary and runtime metrics
checkOutcomes.evidence: A single-state heap summary shows no Detached* constructor among dominant populations, and source/runtime probes found no interval/listener accumulation signal.

principleOutcomes.reason: The principle is contextual and all checks were judged not applicable for this catalogue.

paths.description: Homepage: entry, latest updates, category navigation, preferences, mobile layout, performance, privacy, and crawler rendering.
2026 year listing: representative collection/index template and pagination.
Red Eye detail: representative movie entity template, poster, metadata, synopsis, and first flow step.
Primary journey from movie detail through edition, resolution, and file-variant choices. Stopped before media download.
Recent updates: representative chronological/list feed template.
Deliberate unknown route: representative HTTP failure and recovery state.

findings.summary: The site ignores the system dark-theme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot and computed-style probe remain light: body background rgb(249,249,249), root color-scheme normal, and no color-scheme meta.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare light and dark support and retint page tokens with color-scheme and prefers-color-scheme/light-dark().

findings.summary: High-contrast preferences receive no explicit adaptation.
findings.evidence: The prefers-contrast screenshot is pixel-identical to the default capture, the stylesheet has no prefers-contrast/forced-colors rule, and Lighthouse found low-contrast text.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors/prefers-contrast handling and avoid fixed colors that erase platform contrast adjustments.

findings.summary: Cross-page navigation swaps abruptly.
findings.evidence: The representative MPA flow changes documents with no @view-transition rule; captures show hard page swaps between listing, detail, and download-option pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Use an opt-in cross-document View Transition, with a reduced-motion-safe fallback.

findings.summary: The long homepage provides no scroll-state guidance.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout is 4,161px tall, but DOM/CSS inspection found no sticky progress, scroll-state query, or other position cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight progress or section-position cue for this long catalogue page.

findings.summary: Navigation does not clearly cue the destination or current state.
findings.evidence: Twenty prominent links repeat the label “Download Now”, and the active pagination link uses href="#"; users get little destination or current-state context.
findings.suggestedFix: Use movie-specific link names, aria-current for pagination, and clear transition/focus cues after navigation.

findings.summary: Repetitive promotional and keyword chrome competes with the catalogue.
findings.evidence: The first viewport repeats branding, bookmark/search copy, keyword-heavy prose, and promotional text before the latest titles; every template ends with a Page Keywords block.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove keyword blocks and duplicate brand messaging; lead with search/browse content and the current title.

findings.summary: Reusable catalogue components respond only to the viewport.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no container-type or @container despite folder, movie, update, and pagination components being reused in differently sized contexts.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable cards/lists containment and size-aware container-query adaptations where their composition changes.

findings.summary: Most links have undersized touch targets.
findings.evidence: The active probe measured many links at only 14–17px high, including all “Download Now” and catalogue folder links; focus is visible but touch hit areas are not comfortably sized.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the whole list row/link tappable and provide at least a comfortable 44px-class hit area without reducing visible focus.

findings.summary: The primary download journey has avoidable steps and ambiguous link labels.
findings.evidence: The exercised path requires home → movie detail → “Original” → resolution → file variant before the final download page; repeated generic “Download Now” labels obscure which title is selected.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose resolution, size, and format choices on the detail page with title-specific action names and a clear breadcrumb/back path.

findings.summary: HTTP errors fall through to an unhelpful server page.
findings.evidence: A deliberate missing route returned HTTP 404 with the raw Apache “Not Found” page and no home link, search, explanation, or recovery action.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a branded 404 that preserves navigation and offers search, home, and recent titles.

findings.summary: Mobile LCP and detail-page CLS miss the good Core Web Vitals range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 3.9s on home and 4.0s on detail; detail CLS was 0.126. The first-party trace was faster (LCP 1.18s) with 0 TBT, showing network/device sensitivity rather than main-thread saturation.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP content, shorten render-blocking chains, reserve media space, and verify under mobile throttling.

findings.summary: The poster shifts layout because its dimensions are not reserved.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse attributed a 0.126 CLS shift to the detail page, and the poster img has no width/height attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic width/height (or aspect-ratio) on poster and folder imagery so layout is reserved before load.

findings.summary: Render-blocking CSS/font work delays first paint.
findings.evidence: HAR and Lighthouse identify style.min.css plus the imported Google Fonts stylesheet as render-blocking, with an estimated 1.9s saving; the font request adds a cross-origin dependency.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline minimal critical CSS, replace @import with explicit preconnected font loading, and cache immutable assets.

findings.summary: Third-party JavaScript dominates the otherwise tiny page.
findings.evidence: The HAR transfers 152,784 bytes for gtag alone; Lighthouse estimates 67 KiB unused, while 178,250 of 193,958 transferred bytes are third-party.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove nonessential third-party scripts or load privacy-preserving analytics only after consent/idle when justified.

findings.summary: Text and essential UI colors fail WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured red rating text at 3.79:1 and white “Page Keywords” text at 2.7:1, below 4.5:1 for 14px text.
findings.suggestedFix: Use darker foregrounds or stronger backgrounds and verify every state at WCAG AA contrast.

findings.summary: Pages omit core landmarks and detail templates omit a heading.
findings.evidence: The probe found zero main and nav landmarks; discoverability found zero h1 elements on the movie detail template. Keyboard focus itself remained visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap primary content in main, identify navigation, and use the movie title as the detail-page h1.

findings.summary: Dense 14px copy and repetitive prose reduce scanability.
findings.evidence: Screenshots show long keyword-dense blocks, minimal paragraph spacing, and many nearly identical update rows rendered at 14px.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase base text size and spacing, constrain readable line lengths, and rewrite or remove repetitive keyword copy.

findings.summary: Zoom-capable pages still expose undersized interactive targets.
findings.evidence: Viewport scaling is allowed and 360px layouts do not overflow, but the probe found catalogue links only 14px high and action links 17px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase link padding and spacing so reflowed and zoomed interaction remains comfortable.

findings.summary: Document assets are not consistently dimensioned or responsive.
findings.evidence: The doctype and UTF-8 charset are valid, but the detail image audit found two images without width/height, a 350px JPG displayed at 153px, and no responsive source.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic dimensions and responsive modern image sources; keep the valid document metadata.

findings.summary: Browser diagnostics report preventable platform hygiene failures.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports three BFCache failure reasons plus Cookie issues from xm.viragocosech.com and unwrapsstow.cyou; the HAR records the ad script blocked by ORB.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the failing ad chain and address BFCache blockers; keep third-party browser issues out of the critical path.

findings.summary: Link text is repetitive and one active-page link is not crawlable.
findings.evidence: The homepage contains twenty “Download Now” links with no title in their accessible text; listing page 1 uses href="#" instead of an aria-current non-link or a real URL.
findings.suggestedFix: Use descriptive title-specific link text and model the current page with aria-current rather than a fragment placeholder.

findings.summary: Canonical and sitemap indexing signals are missing.
findings.evidence: All sampled pages returned 200 and robots allows general search indexing, but no canonical link is present and /sitemap.xml returns 404.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish canonical URLs and a sitemap consistent with robots and all public archetypes.

findings.summary: Movie pages lack structured entity and share-preview metadata.
findings.evidence: The movie detail probe found no JSON-LD and no Open Graph metadata despite exposing a named Movie entity, poster, cast, rating, and synopsis.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Movie JSON-LD plus Open Graph/Twitter title, description, image, and canonical URL.

findings.summary: Session cookies and transport defenses are insecurely configured.
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used, but CSP, HSTS, nosniff, framing, referrer, and permissions headers are all absent. PHPSESSID lacks Secure, HttpOnly, and an explicit safe SameSite posture.
findings.suggestedFix: Immediately set Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax on the session cookie and stage CSP/HSTS/nosniff/frame/referrer/permissions headers.

findings.summary: Tracking and an opaque ad script load without an evident consent choice.
findings.evidence: The page contacts five third-party origins, including Google Analytics and xm.viragocosech.com; third parties account for 178,250 of 193,958 transferred bytes, and Lighthouse observes additional third-party cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the opaque ad chain and make any justified analytics minimal, transparent, consent-aware, and short-lived.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: Headers inspection found no clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, HSTS, or CSP frame-ancestors.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy low-risk companion headers now, then roll out nonce/hash CSP in report-only mode before enforcement.

findings.summary: A missing route has no resilient recovery experience.
findings.evidence: The representative 404 is a bare Apache server response with no site context or recovery controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Handle 404 and network errors in the site template with useful retry, search, and navigation actions.

findings.summary: Markup and layout are not prepared for alternate writing directions.
findings.evidence: html lang="en" is present, but dir is implicit and the shared CSS uses physical margin-right and padding-left rules alongside a few logical properties.
findings.suggestedFix: Set direction intentionally where needed and replace physical left/right spacing with logical properties.

findings.summary: Visible dates are not exposed as locale-aware machine-readable data.
findings.evidence: The detail renders “10 February 2025” as a plain span; the probe found no time elements or locale-aware markup across sampled pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit ISO datetime values in time elements and format display dates with Intl for the selected locale.

findings.summary: Several labelled destinations are deceptive or broken.
findings.evidence: “Telegram Update Page”, “Contact Us”, and “DMCA” all point to the homepage, while an opaque third-party ad script loads in the background.
findings.suggestedFix: Point labels to the promised destinations, remove disguised/broken actions, and disclose or remove advertising behavior.

findings.summary: Poster delivery wastes bytes and misses responsive formats.
findings.evidence: The image audit flags the 350px JPG as oversized at a 153px display width with no srcset; Lighthouse estimates 65 KiB image-delivery savings on detail.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP poster variants and a width-based srcset sized to the rendered card.

findings.summary: Background analytics and ad work is disproportionate to page value.
findings.evidence: A static catalogue loads 178,250 bytes of third-party resources and issues analytics/ad requests before user interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Eliminate the opaque ad script and defer any essential analytics until consent/idle with batching.

findings.summary: Third-party code consumes nearly the entire page budget.
findings.evidence: Third-party resources are 91.9% of transferred bytes (178,250/193,958); GTM alone is 152,784 bytes versus 15,708 first-party bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a strict third-party byte budget and keep only scripts with demonstrated user value.

taskList.title: Secure session cookies and deploy browser defense headers
Remove or strictly gate opaque ad and analytics third parties
Make all catalogue rows comfortable, descriptive touch targets
Fix contrast and add preference-driven dark/high-contrast themes
Reserve and responsively deliver poster imagery
Shorten the primary journey and remove deceptive/broken labels
Simplify repetitive keyword chrome and improve text layout
Add semantic landmarks, headings, canonicals, sitemap, and Movie metadata
Add modern navigation and component responsiveness
Make dates and directional layout internationalisation-ready
